extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys, judges, and law students studying equitable remedies for patent infringement
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and rules governing preliminary and perpetual injunctions in patent cases, the use of attachment for contempt, penalties for violations, consent decrees, suspension/dissolution, and the relation of contractual rights to patent remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: No re‑litigation of patent construction in contempt proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: On a motion for attachment for contempt no evidence can be admitted to vary the construction already given to the patent by the court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The only point at issue is the defendant's performance of the forbidden acts; that may be examined by the court or through experts or other witnesses. Cases: Bardett v. Estey; Bann. & A. 141.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachment for contempt may be granted without new suit when injunction violated
rubrics_metrics.description: A motion for attachment for contempt will be granted without a new suit if an injunction is violated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Wetherell v. New Jersey Zinc Co. (1874) and related authorities cited in text; attachments provide summary relief to enforce injunctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachment inappropriate when new questions of identity, validity, or differing acts arise
rubrics_metrics.description: If the alleged violation consists of acts in some respects dissimilar to those described in the injunction or presents a new question of identity between defendant's device and the patented invention, the matter cannot be investigated on application for attachment and requires new pleadings in a supplemental bill or separate action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also applies where defendant acts under a new patent or where justification demands re‑examination of the scope and meaning of the plaintiff's patent; attachment is intended only for summary relief where the single issue is commission of the prohibited acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavits and interrogatories must be specific in contempt motions
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits accompanying a motion for attachment must state the specific acts or omissions constituting the contempt, and interrogatories addressed to the defendant must be confined to these specific offences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defendant need not answer matters charged on information and belief; demurrer to improper interrogatories can recover costs. See Parkhurst v. Kinsman and related cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court will not grant attachment where infringement is genuinely in dispute
rubrics_metrics.description: No attachment will issue where the defendant denies that he is using the plaintiff's process and the court is divided on that point; if the infringement is in dispute a supplemental bill or new suit must be filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cases: California Artificial Stone Paving Co. v. Molitor; Allis v. Stowell; Putnam v. Hollender.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachment only when violation is clear and defendant intended to violate injunction
rubrics_metrics.description: Equity will never proceed for contempt unless the violation of the injunction is clear and proven; the court must have no substantial doubt that the defendant intended to violate the injunction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'clear case' standard is required; see Allis v. Stowell and other authorities cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: No attachment if injunction was procured by plaintiff's strategy or fraud to entrap
rubrics_metrics.description: An order for attachment will not issue if the injunction was procured by strategy, or its violation was induced by the fraud of the plaintiff for the purpose of entrapping and punishing the defendant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts will refuse attachment where there is reasonable ground to doubt the wrongfulness of defendant's conduct (Bate Refrigerating Co. v. Gillett; California Artificial Stone Paving Co. v. Molitor).

rubrics_metrics.name: Service/notice requirement for attachment motions
rubrics_metrics.description: An attachment for contempt will not be granted unless notice of the motion has been served on the defendant, and the infringement complained of is committed either by him or by persons under his control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Sickels v. Borden; Bate Refrigerating Co. v. Gillett.

rubrics_metrics.name: No attachment against one who was not a party to the suit with notice
rubrics_metrics.description: No attachment will be ordered against one who was not a party to the suit with notice of the injunction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service/party status is essential; see Sickels v. Borden (1857).

rubrics_metrics.name: Plaintiff may use agents to test for ongoing violations if no artifice or falsehood
rubrics_metrics.description: After an injunction is granted, the patentee may send persons to buy of the defendant to see if he is violating the injunction; such sending is not an implied license to the defendant to sell.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permissible so long as patentee does not resort to artifice or falsehood; report of such a person is privileged and not ground for slander (Knowles v. Peck).

rubrics_metrics.name: Court may examine infringement itself or use experts on attachment motion
rubrics_metrics.description: On a motion for attachment the court may, at its discretion, examine the fact of infringement by itself or may have experts, but its decision on this question does not prejudice the parties on the accounting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Burdett v. Estey and Bann. & A. 141; availability of expert aid is discretionary.

rubrics_metrics.name: No attachment while validity of agreement under which injunction obtained is disputed in another court
rubrics_metrics.description: No attachment will be ordered while the validity of an agreement under which the injunction was obtained is disputed in a State court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equity abstains where key collateral questions are being litigated elsewhere (Pentlarge v. Beeston and authorities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary injunction: order of attachment only where violation is clear and reasonable doubt absent
rubrics_metrics.description: An order for attachment will not issue unless the violation of the injunction is clear, nor even then if there is reasonable ground to doubt the wrongfulness of the defendant's conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court balances clarity of violation against reason to doubt; see Bate Refrigerating Co. v. Gillett and California Artificial Stone Paving Co. v. Molitor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalty for contempt: fine or imprisonment discretionary; measure by damages and costs
rubrics_metrics.description: A defendant found guilty of contempt in violating an injunction may be punished by fine or imprisonment in the discretion of the court; the amount of the fine is measured in ordinary cases by the damage the plaintiff sustained through the defendant's disobedience, to which costs and legal expenses of the attachment application may be added.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court may refer facts to a master for computation; bad faith or contumacy may increase penalty; mitigation factors include defendant's pecuniary situation, domestic difficulties, and plaintiff's motive. Cases: Potter v. Muller; Ready Roofing Co. v. Taylor; Goodyear v. Mullee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committal for non‑payment is incidental and payment ends commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: When the fine is paid there can be no commitment, or if paid after commitment the defendant is entitled to be released; the commitment for non‑payment is incidental to the judgment for a fine and not a separate imprisonment punishment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment of the fine is the punishment; civil nature of order for commitment; commitment may be suspended for appeal on bond. Authorities: Fischer v. Hayes and related case law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civil character of commitment for non‑payment and appeal limits
rubrics_metrics.description: An order for commitment for non‑payment of a fine on contempt is a civil order, not a criminal sentence; no appeal lies to the Supreme Court on a contempt proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Hendryx v. Fitzpatrick; Hayes v. Fischer (102 U.S. 121).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary injunction violation without willfulness limits remedy to profits/damages and motion costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the violation of a preliminary injunction is not wilful and the object of the motion for attachment is to find out whether the defendant really infringes, he is liable only for the profits or damages and the costs of the motion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mitigates harsh penalties where good faith showing exists; authorities include Ready Roofing Co. v. Taylor and Schillinger v. Gunther.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perpetual injunction routinely granted on final decree if patent still in force
rubrics_metrics.description: A perpetual injunction issues, as a matter of course, at the conclusion of a suit in equity whenever the plaintiff has sustained the allegations of his bill, provided the patent has not then expired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is granted irrespective of right to profits or damages. If one of several patents/claims in the action is valid while others are void, an injunction on the valid claim will be ordered. See Potter v. Mack; Colgate v. International Ocean Tel. Co.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perpetual injunction independent of award of profits or damages
rubrics_metrics.description: The right to an injunction is independent of the right to profits or damages; courts may enjoin future acts though legal compensation might be adequate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equitable relief is fitted to the threatened wrong; injunction prohibits defendant from future undertaking during the monopoly's continuance. See Colgate v. International Ocean Tel. Co.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration of perpetual injunction: limited to life of patent except re: infringing articles made during term
rubrics_metrics.description: A perpetual injunction is operative only during the life of the patent and should be expressly limited thereto, except in reference to infringing articles constructed while the patent was in force and capable of use after it has expired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts should phrase decrees to reflect patent term; where infringing articles were made during term, injunction against their use may be decreed post‑expiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of injunctions and appellate effect
rubrics_metrics.description: A perpetual injunction may be suspended till acceptance of the master's report or to allow appeal in the court's discretion; an appeal to the Supreme Court does not of itself suspend or supersede the injunction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In deciding suspension courts consider special hardship, public necessity, contracts with third parties, and must protect interests of all parties. The imminent expiry of a patent alone is not sufficient ground for suspension. See Potter v. Mack; Brown v. Deere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perpetual injunction by consent allowed but limited; collusive consent will be set aside
rubrics_metrics.description: The court may issue a perpetual injunction by consent of the defendant unless the action or decree are evidently collusive; in such cases it will not pass upon patentability or validity to influence future litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If terms of consent are disputed a final hearing will be had and the case reopened; a decree by consent is not a general decree allowing attachment on mere motion — a bill must be filed and issues raised for contempt. Collusive suits will be dismissed. See Tomkinson v. Willetts Mfg. Co.; Roemer v. Neumann.

rubrics_metrics.name: Violation and dissolution of perpetual injunction governed by same principles as preliminary injunction contempt
rubrics_metrics.description: A perpetual injunction may be violated by acts which under a preliminary injunction would be contempt; redress and penalties follow the rules stated for that offence. Dissolution rests on same principles and may be ordered within two years after entering the decree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enforcement, penalties, and dissolution applications follow the established equitable rules earlier described in the treatise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights under contracts concerning patented inventions rest on general contract law; assignment vs license distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: Reciprocal rights of assignors/assignees and grantors/grantees rest upon express or implied contracts and the general law of contracts; an assignment conveys the monopoly (property) whereas a license creates no property but is a simple agreement not to enforce the prohibitions of the monopoly against the licensee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This distinction affects available remedies, warranties, estoppels, and enforcement; treatise collects cases to illustrate these doctrines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breach of contract by licensee/assignee that infringes is actionable both as breach and as tort
rubrics_metrics.description: Wrongs committed by contracting parties which include infringement of the patent constitute breaches of contract; when a contracting party exceeds privileges conferred by his license or conveyance, liability may rest on both contract and tort bases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The same person may be both licensee/assignee and a stranger for different acts; remedies may include contract suit or tort action for interference with property rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: No attachment where defendant acts under new patent granted since injunction
rubrics_metrics.description: A motion for attachment for contempt will not be granted if the defendant is acting under a new patent granted since the injunction issued; a new hearing must be had.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires reconsideration because the legal justification for the defendant's acts changed after injunction entry. Cases: Wirt v. Brown; Onderdonk v. Fanning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order adjudging contempt need not aver legality of injunction if affidavits/reports show offence
rubrics_metrics.description: The order adjudging the contempt need not aver that the injunction was lawful, nor recite the offence where the affidavits and reports filed do so and the order refers thereto.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural flexibility recognized; see Fischer v. Hayes and related authorities.
